subject: Qualification → POC alignment & access roadmap (ScoutingHouse)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Moreno <claire@scoutinghouse.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@scoutinghouse.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Qualification → POC alignment & access roadmap (ScoutingHouse)

Thanks for the time today — appreciate the candid run-through of your current flow. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the proposed POC scope, measurable success criteria, owners, and the access items we’ll need to start. Please confirm or correct anything I’ve mis‑captured.

Key pain points (as described)
- Manual review of user-reported incidents takes ~3.5 FTE hours/day; backlog grows during peak windows.
- High false-positive rate in current classifier (~40%) which drives unnecessary escalations.
- Slow summarization for long threads; agents lose context and need to re-open tickets.

Top goals for the POC
1) Reduce manual triage time by 30–40% on the ticket queue segment selected for the pilot.
2) Improve classifier precision so false positives drop to <20%.
3) Produce concise 2–3 line summaries for long ticket threads with human-acceptable quality in 80% of samples.

Proposed POC scope (3 weeks, isolated dataset)
- Model surface: intent classification + thread summarization (single runbook).
- Data: 2,000 historical tickets (anonymized sample) + 30 canonical prompts for evaluation.
- Evaluation: 100 blind evals (50 classification, 50 summarization) scored by your SME group.
- Runtime: hosted Redwood inference on dedicated test pool; we’ll instrument latency and token-cost.

Success metrics (pass/fail gating)
- Classification: precision >= 0.80 on the blind eval set.
- Summaries: average human rating >= 4/5 on quality rubric for the 50 evals.
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 300 ms for single-shot summarization for our test size.
- Cost: target token costs not to exceed $0.09 per processed ticket in POC configuration (we’ll provide tuning knobs).

Owners & roles
- Account lead: Irene Choi (Redwood) — commercial/roadmap decisions.
- Engineering lead: Marcus Lin (Redwood) — infra/endpoint config and SLOs.
- Solutions Eng: Aditya Rao (Redwood) — prompt engineering, eval harness.
- Customer SME / POC owner: Claire Moreno (ScoutingHouse).

Timeline (high-level)
- Today (Mon 6/29): alignment and confirmation of scope & access items.
- Wed 7/1: customer delivers anonymized sample and S3 path (or shared Drive) + list of SME evaluators.
- Fri 7/3: Redwood delivers POC runbook + initial prompt set (attachment).
- Mon 7/6: Technical kickoff (30–45m) — infra + onboarding.
- Week of 7/6–7/17: POC run, regular check-ins Tue/Thu.
- Fri 7/17: Deliver evaluation report and final recommendation.

Access & security checklist (what we need to get started)
1) A sample dataset: 2k anonymized tickets, CSV with columns: ticket_id, text, metadata. (attachment: sample-prompts.csv)
2) S3 read-only path OR a Google Drive folder (please confirm preferred).
3) Option A (preferred): an IAM role for Redwood with read-only access to the S3 path.
   Option B: temporary upload to an encrypted Drive link (we’ll supply upload instructions).
4) Network allowlist: IP range for Redwood test pool (we’ll provide CIDR).
5) Contact for procurement/NDA if required (include PO contact).

Attachments included: scoping-runbook_v1.xlsx, redwood-poc-access-checklist.pdf, sample-prompts.csv

Immediate asks (actions & owners)
- Claire/Raj: confirm scope & timeline by Tue 6/30 EOD. (Claire)
- Claire: share a staging S3 path or Drive link + list of evaluators by Wed 7/1.
- Marcus: will send the allowlist CIDR and temporary service account template by Tue 6/30. (Marcus)
- Aditya: will attach the eval rubric and initial prompt seed by Fri 7/3. (Aditya)

If this looks good I’ll schedule the technical kickoff for Mon 7/6 and circulate a calendar invite. Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com | +1 415‑555‑0142

From: Claire Moreno <claire@scoutinghouse.ai>

Subject: Re: Qualification → POC alignment & access roadmap (ScoutingHouse)

Thanks Irene — this is a helpful summary and I think you captured the priorities. A couple quick clarifications from my side before we lock dates: 

1) Data residency: our legal team will only allow EU data to be processed in-region for EU customers. We are US-headquartered but some of the tickets are EU-resident. For the POC, can Redwood guarantee that EU-data will be processed in an EU region?

2) Audit/SOC2 evidence: we’ll need a SOC2 Type II snapshot and a standard security questionnaire answered before we share the full dataset. Can you point me to the right contact for that?

3) For the evaluation rubric — can you confirm whether the blind evals will be double-blind (i.e., reviewers won’t know which outputs were model vs. baseline)? We prefer double-blind for unbiased scoring.

We’re also OK with a 3‑week window as long as the kickoff stays on or before 7/6. I’ll confirm evaluators and try to provide a Drive link by Wed 7/1.

Quick note — I’ll loop in our Procurement lead (Suresh Iyer) if we need an NDA/PO.

Best,
Claire
Claire Moreno
Head of Product Ops | ScoutingHouse
claire@scoutinghouse.ai

Hi Claire — quick responses inline to your questions and a few technical notes on access.

1) Data residency: Redwood supports region-specific serving. For POC we can route requests to the EU test pool (Frankfurt) if your dataset is tagged as EU. That requires the S3 bucket to be in the same region (or for us to use a customer-owned EU bucket and role). We’ll document the region routing in the runbook.

2) SOC2 / security evidence: you can get the SOC2 snapshot and our security pack from security@redwoodinference.com. I’ll copy the standard questionnaire we use for POCs in a separate email (or attach if preferred).

3) Blind evals: we recommend a double-blind setup — Redwood will randomize outputs and produce an eval sheet that hides model labels. We’ll also include a baseline model (your current classifier) so reviewers score model vs baseline without labels.

Access steps — minimal steps to get started (technical)
- Option 1 (recommended): Create a customer IAM role with read-only access to the S3 prefix "s3://scoutinghouse-poc/2026-sample" and grant assume-role to redwood-poc@redwoodinference.com. We’ll provide the role ARN template.
- Option 2: Drop encrypted archive to Drive link and share link with redwood-poc@redwoodinference.com (less ideal for residency guarantees).
- We’ll need 1–2 sample tickets with schema and a data dictionary so we can map fields.

Notes on logging/retention: for the POC we can either (a) keep logs ephemeral (no retention beyond 48 hours) or (b) forward logs to your customer S3 for retention. If you choose (b) we’ll provide a KMS key policy example.

I’ll send the role template and eval rubric by EOD. Happy to jump on a short call with your infra owner if helpful.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwoodinference.com
